captions.text: All right, let us put the scene right in
front of you. It is early May in Transennsylvania.
Jonathan Harker, a young English solicitor, sits in that
firelit, oppressive room after a well,
just a terrifying journey through the Carpathian Mountains.
Right. He's completely isolated.
Exactly. He is miles from anything resembling modern civilization.
And he lays the deed to the Carfax estate
on the count's table and the count signs them.
He takes the pen and signs them.
This proves the monster's first act in England is
a signature. He doesn't arrive as a conquering warlord
reigning fire on the beaches.
You know, he enters society through property law.
Yeah, but you were looking at the ink and
you are completely ignoring the entity holding the pen.
How so? The signature is just a meaningless formality
to him. We are talking about a monster of
prodigious physical strength. Oh, sure.
He's strong. Strong. This is a creature who Harker
later watches climb face down the sheer outer walls
of his castle. Oh, that scene is wild, right?
